chosen.premise: When bird Pokémon target Caterpie, Butterfree drives them away by sprinkling toxic scales.
chosen.hook: Butterfree has a terrifying answer for Caterpie hunters.
chosen.visualIdea: A bird silhouette swoops toward Caterpie before Butterfree blocks the path with a sparkling cloud of scales.
chosen.note: The protective relationship is unusually specific, dramatic, and directly supported: Butterfree uses toxic scales to drive off birds attacking Caterpie.

candidates.premise: At level 7 Caterpie becomes Metapod, then just three levels later it becomes the flying Butterfree at level 10.
candidates.hook: Metapod only waits three levels before it gets wings.
candidates.visualIdea: A level meter climbs from 7 to 10 as Caterpie becomes Metapod, then cracks open into airborne Butterfree.
candidates.note: The three-level countdown is clear and easy to animate, but evolution timing is a familiar Pokémon fact and less surprising than the bodyguard behavior.

candidates.premise: Gigantamax Butterfree reaches 17 meters—over 15 times the height of its normal 1.1-meter form.
candidates.hook: Butterfree can grow from 1.1 meters to 17.
candidates.visualIdea: Normal Butterfree stands beside a height scale, then Gigantamax Butterfree towers past it at 17 meters.
candidates.note: The scale comparison is highly visual and numerically solid, though Gigantamax size comparisons are a broad Pokémon format rather than uniquely Butterfree.

candidates.premise: Butterfree’s wings release toxic dust, yet their poisonous powder also repels rain so it can keep flying.
candidates.hook: Butterfree’s toxic wings are also built for rain.
candidates.visualIdea: Toxic dust bursts from flapping wings, then rain beads and rolls harmlessly off in slow motion.
candidates.note: A strong contradiction between poisonous scales and rain resistance, though the core idea is slightly less distinctive than Butterfree’s other behaviors.

candidates.premise: Butterfree can seek, extract, and carry honey from flowers blooming over six miles from its nest.
candidates.hook: Butterfree will fly over six miles for honey.
candidates.visualIdea: A map line stretches six miles from a nest to a tiny flower, ending with Butterfree hauling honey home.
candidates.note: The six-mile distance is concrete and memorable; the map visualization works, but the research says it can seek and carry honey from that distance rather than explicitly describing a six-mile flight.

candidates.premise: Butterfree’s large eyes look simple from afar, but each one is composed of a myriad of tiny eyes.
candidates.hook: Zoom into Butterfree’s eye—and it becomes countless eyes.
candidates.visualIdea: An extreme camera zoom enters one large eye and reveals a dense mosaic of tiny individual eyes.
candidates.note: Extremely Butterfree-specific and visually striking, but 'myriad' is vague and the reveal is more of a visual fact than a fully developed episode premise.
